name: PasswordInput

examples.title: In a Form
New Passwords
examples.code:
<PasswordInput
  label="New password"
  autoComplete="new-password"
  message="At least 15 characters."
/>

examples.title: Translating
examples.code:
<PasswordInput
  label="Contraseña"
  variant="text"
  labels={{
    showPassword: 'Mostrar contraseña',
    hidePassword: 'Ocultar contraseña',
    show: 'Mostrar',
    hide: 'Ocultar',
  }}
/>

examples.title: Showing Two Fields Together
Sizes, Colors and a Left Icon
examples.code:
<>
  <PasswordInput label="Small" size="small" />
  <PasswordInput label="Medium, as words" size="medium" variant="text" />
  <PasswordInput
    label="With an icon"
    iconLeftName="lock"
    isRounded
    color="danger"
    message="That password isn't right."
    messageColor="danger"
  />
</>

examples.title: Strength Recipe

accessibility:
- **The input** is a password field named by its `label`, and a text field while the password shows. Switching keeps its value and the selection.
- **The icon button** is a toggle button: it's named "Show password" in both states, and `aria-pressed` says whether the password shows, so a screen reader hears "Show password, toggle button, pressed". The eye takes a line through it while the password shows, and the glyphs are hidden from assistive tech.
- **The text button** changes its words, so its name changes with them, "Show password" then "Hide password", and it has no `aria-pressed`, as the [APG button pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/button/) asks of a toggle whose label changes. Each name contains the word on the button ([Label in Name](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/label-in-name.html)).
- **Keyboard:** the button is a native `<button type="button">` in the tab order, right after the input, and Enter or Space toggles it and leaves focus on it. It never submits the form.
- **Pointer:** a press on the button leaves focus, and the caret, in the input.
- **No announcement of its own:** the button's state or its name says whether the password shows, so there's no live region repeating it.
- **Password managers and paste** work as on any password field, and `autocomplete` tells them what the field is for ([Identify Input Purpose](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/identify-input-purpose.html)). `spellcheck="false"` keeps a browser's spellcheck from reading the password once it shows.
- **The `value` attribute:** a controlled field carries its value in its `value` attribute, as React writes it for any controlled input, where a CSS attribute selector can read it. An uncontrolled one, read with `FormData`, never puts what's typed there.
- **Edge's own reveal button** is hidden on this input, so there's one eye, not two.
- **Focus** shows as an outline around the button. **Forced colors:** the glyph and the words take the system's button text color, and a disabled button its gray.
- **Strings** come from `labels`, with English defaults.
summary: The `PasswordInput` component is a password field with a button inside it that shows what was typed. By default the button is an eye named "Show password" that reports whether the password shows with `aria-pressed`; `variant="text"` makes it the words "Show" and "Hide". The field asks for `autocomplete="current-password"` and no spellcheck, and hides the password again when its form submits.

parts.summary: The `PasswordInput` component is a password field with a button inside it that shows what was typed. By default the button is an eye named "Show password" that reports whether the password shows with `aria-pressed`; `variant="text"` makes it the words "Show" and "Hide". The field asks for `autocomplete="current-password"` and no spellcheck, and hides the password again when its form submits.

props.name: label
props.description: Field label. Automatically associated with the input via `htmlFor`, using your `id` when provided, otherwise a generated one. Dropped inside an outer `Field`, whose own label associates instead when that `Field` generates a target id (not `grouped`/`hasAddons`, no explicit `labelProps.htmlFor`) and you set no `id` here.

props.name: labelProps
props.description: Props for the label element when the component renders its own `Field`; dropped inside an outer `Field` (use that `Field`'s `labelProps` instead). An explicit `htmlFor` key, even `undefined`, overrides the automatic association and no id is generated.

props.name: iconLeft
props.description: Icon props for the left icon. Bulma gives control icons `pointer-events: none`, so a clickable node here never receives a click.

props.name: iconLeftName
props.description: Shortcut for the left icon's name.

props.name: iconLeftSize
props.description: Shortcut for the left icon's size.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows a loading spinner on the `Control` it renders, at the edge the toggle uses, so the toggle isn't drawn meanwhile. Inside your own `Control` it renders none, so this draws nothing and warns in development; set `isLoading` on that `Control`, which hides the toggle too.

props.name: fieldClassName
props.description: Additional CSS classes for the Field.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Additional CSS classes for the Control.

props.name: visible
props.description: Whether the password shows, when you hold the state. Setting it makes the visibility controlled: the toggle only calls `onVisibleChange`, and so does hiding again on its own. Apply that `false` and the field is a password field by the time the form reads it; keep `visible` true and the field stays shown.

props.name: defaultVisible
props.description: Whether the password shows at first, when the input holds its own state.

props.name: onVisibleChange
props.description: Called with the new visibility on each toggle, and with `false` when the form submits or resets, or the page is left, which it also is on the way into the back-forward cache. React renders those hides at once, a state update you make here included, so the form reads a password field. One that fires while React is rendering or running layout effects, such as a `requestSubmit()` from a layout effect, can't render there, and lands just after.

props.name: variant
props.description: How the toggle draws itself: an eye icon with a fixed name and `aria-pressed`, or the words "Show" and "Hide" with a name that follows them.

props.name: labels
props.type: { showPassword?: string; hidePassword?: string; show?: string; hide?: string }

props.name: color
props.description: Bulma color modifier for the input.

props.name: isStatic
props.description: Styles the input as static text. It stays editable; add `readOnly` to stop edits.

extraProps.name: autoComplete
extraProps.description: Tells the browser and password managers this is an existing password. Pass `"new-password"` where the user makes one up, on a sign-up or change-password form.

extraProps.name: spellCheck
extraProps.description: Off, so a browser's spellcheck never sees the password once it shows.

extraProps.name: autoCorrect
extraProps.description: Off, so a phone's keyboard doesn't change what's typed.

extraProps.name: autoCapitalize
extraProps.description: Off, so a phone's keyboard doesn't capitalize the first letter.

extraProps.name: value
extraProps.description: The password, controlled. React writes a controlled input's value into its `value` attribute, as it does on any input, so the password sits in the page's markup. Uncontrolled, read with `FormData`, the field never puts what's typed there.
